content.text:
Those modules are fetched by a full module-graph command, not by building or testing Kit. `go test` of the Modal provider does not download or compile them.

The Modal provider imports `google.golang.org/grpc`. The published `google.golang.org/grpc` v1.83.2 `go.mod` requires `gonum.org/v1/gonum` and `github.com/spiffe/go-spiffe/v2` for gRPC's own tests. Go has a single `require` block, so any import of gRPC puts those modules in the module graph. A package load records their `go.mod` checksums and stops there. It does not compile them.

`go work sync` and `go list -m all` go further. They read every `go.mod` in that graph. SPIFFE's `go.mod` requires `google.golang.org/grpc/examples`. Gonum's `go.mod` requires the plot, PDF, and font modules. Each `go.mod` the command reads is downloaded, and because `go.work` is present, the checksum is appended to `go.work.sum`. `go mod tidy` updates a module's own `go.sum` and leaves `go.work.sum` unchanged, so those extra checksums stayed in the last commit.

`go.work.sum` is now the 57 checksums that loading the workspace packages actually writes. `sandbox-kit test go` rebuilds that set and fails if the file contains anything else. Update dependencies inside the module with `GOWORK=off`, using `go get` and then `go mod tidy`.

input.command:
git push -u origin HEAD && gh pr edit 37 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Daytona and Modal share one filesystem on the sandbox handle. Lifecycle stays on the handle. The eight calls are read, write, copy in, copy out, make a directory, list one directory, stat, and remove.
- A sandbox path must be absolute. A relative path fails in Kit before either provider is contacted. Read and write move bytes. Copy uses a path on the caller's disk.
- `parents` defaults to true, so creating a directory also creates missing parents. Set it to false when the parent must already exist. Daytona rejects that value. Modal requires the parent and returns an error if the new directory is already there.
- TypeScript Daytona read, write, and copy pass a timeout as a whole number of seconds. `2000` is two seconds. `1500` is rejected, and the field is `timeout`. An omitted timeout on those four calls is passed as `0`, so Daytona adds no transfer limit and the abort signal carries the client deadline. Directory, list, metadata, and delete calls use the abort signal, so `1500` ends the call at 1.5 seconds. Every Go file call uses the context as the deadline. Modal file calls use the context or the abort signal.
- A missing file on copy from the local machine is not found. A local directory is an invalid argument. The field is `local_path`. TypeScript Modal makes that decision before it looks up the sandbox. Copy onto the machine with TypeScript Daytona or Modal creates a missing local parent directory. Go Daytona checks the parent before it downloads. A missing parent is not found, and the field is `local_path`.
- Go Daytona stat and list read the toolbox file record. The result keeps `path`, `permissions`, `owner`, and `group` when Daytona sends them. `modifiedAt` keeps a fractional timestamp. An empty field stays unset, and an unreadable `modifiedAt` is omitted. TypeScript Daytona already mapped those fields.
- Each call has its own Go and TypeScript example. Those examples open a sandbox that already exists and perform that one call.
- `go.work.sum` keeps only the checksums written by loading the workspace packages. `go work sync` and `go list -m all` walk the full `google.golang.org/grpc` requirement graph and download `go.mod` files for modules the build never imports, including plot, PDF, font, and example modules named by gRPC test requirements. `sandbox-kit test go` rebuilds that sum from package loads and fails when the committed file drifts. Update a module's dependencies inside that module with `GOWORK=off` (`go get`, then `go mod tidy`).

## How a call moves

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  caller[Caller]
  files[Filesystem on the handle]
  path[Absolute path check]
  gate[One call at a time on this handle]
  adapter[Daytona or Modal adapter]
  native[Native SDK]

  caller --> files --> path --> gate --> adapter --> native
```

A relative path, a blank path, or a path that contains a NUL byte stops at the path check. The provider is not called. An omitted timeout uses the client deadline. Explicit zero adds no Kit deadline.

TypeScript Daytona read, write, and copy pass the timeout to Daytona as a whole number of seconds. `2000` milliseconds is 2 seconds. `1500` milliseconds is 1.5 seconds, so those calls reject it. The field is `timeout`. An omitted timeout, and an explicit `0`, are passed as `0`. Daytona adds no transfer limit. The abort signal carries the client deadline. A read with that `0` uses Daytona's multi-file download for the one path, because `downloadFile(path, 0)` drops the `0` and keeps Daytona's 30-minute default. `2000` still uses `downloadFile(path, 2)`. `makeDirectory`, `listDirectory`, `stat`, and `remove` use the abort signal, so `1500` ends the call at 1.5 seconds. Every Go file call uses the context as the deadline, so `1500 * time.Millisecond` ends the call at 1.5 seconds. Modal file calls use the context or the abort signal.

## One method, two native calls

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph kit [Sandbox Kit]
    readFile[ReadFile]
    writeFile[WriteFile]
    copyIn[CopyFromLocal]
    copyOut[CopyToLocal]
    mkdir[MakeDirectory]
    listDir[ListDirectory]
    stat[Stat]
    remove[Remove]
  end

  subgraph daytona [Daytona SDK]
    download[DownloadFile]
    upload[UploadFile]
    folder[CreateFolder]
    listFiles[ListFiles]
    details[GetFileInfo]
    deleteFile[DeleteFile]
  end

  subgraph modal [Modal SDK]
    readBytes[ReadBytes]
    writeBytes[WriteBytes]
    fromLocal[CopyFromLocal]
    toLocal[CopyToLocal]
    makeDir[MakeDirectory]
    listFilesM[ListFiles]
    statM[Stat]
    removeM[Remove]
  end

  readFile --> download
  readFile --> readBytes
  writeFile --> upload
  writeFile --> writeBytes
  copyIn --> upload
  copyIn --> fromLocal
  copyOut --> download
  copyOut --> toLocal
  mkdir --> folder
  mkdir --> makeDir
  listDir --> listFiles
  listDir --> listFilesM
  stat --> details
  stat --> statM
  remove --> deleteFile
  remove --> removeM
```

Go Daytona list and stat call the toolbox `ListFiles` and `GetFileInfo` directly. The high-level Daytona file type omits `path` on stat, and it omits `permissions`, `owner`, `group`, and a fractional `modifiedAt` on both calls.

## Creating a directory

`parents` defaults to true. An omitted flag and an explicit true both create missing parents.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  omitted[parents omitted or true]
  strict[parents false]
  daytonaOk[Daytona creates missing parents]
  modalOk[Modal creates missing parents and accepts an existing directory]
  rejected[Daytona rejects the call. Field is parents]
  modalStrict[Modal requires the parent. An existing directory returns an error]

  omitted --> daytonaOk
  omitted --> modalOk
  strict --> rejected
  strict --> modalStrict
```

Modal accepts a directory that already exists when `parents` is true. Daytona returns the provider error when it already exists. `Remove` deletes a file or an empty directory unless `recursive` is set. `Stat` on a symlink describes the symlink. Modal can report a symlink. Daytona reports a file or a directory. `permissions`, `owner`, and `group` are set when the provider supplies them. `modifiedAt` is set when the provider supplies a time.

## Copying a local file

A missing file passed to copy from the local machine is not found before the provider reads it. A directory at that path is an invalid argument. The field is `local_path`. TypeScript Modal does this before `fromId`.

Copy onto the machine with TypeScript Daytona or Modal creates a missing local parent directory. Go Daytona stats the parent first. A missing parent is not found, the field is `local_path`, and the remote file is not downloaded. A local destination that is already a directory is an invalid argument with the same field.

## Where it sits

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  client[Client]
  handle[Sandbox handle]
  life[Lifecycle: start, stop, terminate, delete]
  fs[Filesystem]

  client --> handle
  handle --> life
  handle --> fs
```

Closing the client or the handle does not delete the files or the sandbox.

## Test plan

- [ ] `GOWORK=off go test` in `sdks/go/sandbox`, `sdks/go/providers/daytona`, and `sdks/go/providers/modal`
- [ ] `npm test` in `sdks/typescript/sandbox`, `sdks/typescript/providers/daytona`, and `sdks/typescript/providers/modal`
- [ ] Compile the new Go and TypeScript filesystem examples
- [ ] Confirm a relative sandbox path fails before the provider is called
- [ ] Confirm Daytona rejects `parents: false` before the provider is called, and Modal requires the parent to exist
- [ ] Confirm TypeScript Daytona read, write, and copy reject `1500` milliseconds and pass `2000` as 2 seconds
- [ ] Confirm an omitted TypeScript Daytona read passes `0` through the multi-file download, and write and copy pass `0`
- [ ] Confirm a Go file call and a TypeScript list call accept `1500` milliseconds as the deadline
- [ ] Confirm a missing local file is not found with field `local_path`, and a local directory is an invalid argument with the same field
- [ ] Confirm Go Daytona copy onto a missing parent is not found before the download
- [ ] Confirm Go Daytona stat and list keep `path`, `permissions`, `owner`, `group`, and a fractional `modifiedAt` when Daytona sends them
- [ ] Confirm `sandbox-kit test go` fails when `go.work.sum` contains checksums that loading the workspace packages does not write
